name: Barcelona Cathedral – the religious persecution of 1936
story: In the first months after the military rising was defeated in Barcelona on 19–20 July 1936, a wave of revolutionary violence swept the Republican zone. Priests, monks, nuns and Catholic laypeople were among its main victims, and many churches were burned. Most of the killings were carried out by militia patrols and 'control committees' outside any legal process; the Generalitat and the Republican government gradually reined them in from late 1936. The cathedral is a place to reflect on this violence against the Church in Barcelona in 1936; some of the diocese's clergy killed then have since been beatified.
see: The Gothic cathedral and its cloister on Carrer del Bisbe. Earlier versions of this guide mentioned a memorial chapel to the clergy killed in 1936; it has not been independently confirmed, so ask at the cathedral.
plan: Inside or next to the cathedral; entry to parts of the cathedral requires a ticket outside worship hours; be respectful during services.

vis.label: Open
vis.text: Tourist visit Mon–Fri 09:30–18:30; Sat & religious eves 09:30–17:15; Sun & religious hols 14:00–17:00 (last entry 45 min before)

boxes.text: Nationwide, about 6,800 clergy were killed in the Republican zone (A. Montero's count).
